# Strategy to implement: [water-filling-target-allocation] Proportional water-filling targets with sorted

Mechanism family: water-filling-target-allocation
Replacement scope: Replaces the `target_greedy` construction phase (and the LP-bound `L` targeting) inside `compute_model_placement`; the SA refinement and greedy fallback remain as the incumbent fallback.
Compute budget: One deterministic construction pass per ordering (3 orderings), O(models × gpus) each; negligible evaluation-time increase (<10 ms). No iterative optimizer starts.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's LP bound `L = total_load / total_free` treats free memory as one global pool, so per-GPU targets are implicit rather than explicit. Water-filling instead assigns each GPU an explicit load target `t_g = w_total * free_g / total_free` where `free_g` is computed after a first-fit-decreasing memory packing pass (sizes only, largest model first, into the GPU with most remaining memory). Then models, sorted by `req_rate/slo` descending, are assigned by a two-pointer sweep: each model goes to the GPU whose current load is farthest below its target `t_g` while still fitting memory, with the denominator effect (placing a model shrinks `free_g` and thus the effective target) corrected by recomputing `t_g` after each placement. This yields a globally proportional solution the greedy/SA pipeline cannot reach because greedy is myopic per-model and SA rarely crosses the large rearrangement barrier. Feasibility is preserved by the FFD memory pass and a per-placement fit check; if any model cannot fit, fall back to the incumbent placement.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is the explicit per-GPU load target proportional to actual post-packing headroom, which the incumbent's single global bound `L` cannot express; falsifiable threshold: average max-KVPR strictly below the incumbent's on the benchmark (i.e., printed `Max KVPR` > 26.256), since the water-filling solution provably meets the LP bound whenever the packing phase's headroom distribution matches the load distribution.
